comment: Two faces of one point. (a) "Autonomy and Sovereignty" can be read as building and operating everything nationally, which defeats reuse and cost-control; we suggest clarifying that it means choice, control, and exit/migration rights, in line with the Reusability and Public Governance principles. (b) "Technology-neutral" covers neutral specification and standard interfaces — already in the §3.5.1 bullets — but not the implementation. A neutral spec on a proprietary stack still locks a country in. We recommend adding that implementations use open, non-proprietary technology.

public.text: Two faces of one point. (a) "Autonomy and Sovereignty" can be read as building and operating everything nationally, which defeats reuse and cost-control; we suggest clarifying that it means choice, control, and exit/migration rights, in line with the Reusability and Public Governance principles. (b) "Technology-neutral" covers neutral specification and standard interfaces — already in the §3.5.1 bullets — but not the implementation. A neutral spec on a proprietary stack still locks a country in. We recommend adding that implementations use open, non-proprietary technology.
